name: Slow Cooker Beef Stew
description: Tender chunks of chuck, carrots and potatoes in a rich, thyme-scented gravy. Browning the beef first gives the stew its deep flavour.
ingredients: 2 1/2 lb beef chuck roast, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
1 1/2 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 1 1/2-inch chunks
2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley, for serving
instructions: Pat the beef dry, season it with the salt and pepper, and toss it with the flour until coated.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in two batches without crowding the pan, about 4 minutes per batch, and move it to the slow cooker.

Lower the heat to medium, add the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute, then pour in 1 cup of the broth and scrape up the browned bits from the pan.
Pour the onion mixture into the slow cooker with the rest of the broth, the Worcestershire sauce, thyme, bay leaves, carrots, celery and potatoes. Stir so the beef is mostly covered.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours, or on high for 4 to 5 hours, until the beef falls apart when pressed with a fork.
Remove the bay leaves and stir in the peas. Cover and let them warm through for 5 minutes, then taste, adjust the salt and pepper, and serve sprinkled with parsley.
notes: Browning the beef can be skipped on a busy morning, but it gives the stew most of its depth. Chuck is the cut to use: leaner cuts turn dry and stringy. The stew keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer, and tastes even better the next day.

name: Slow Cooker Chicken Tortilla Soup
description: A smoky, gently spiced chicken soup with black beans and corn, finished with crisp baked tortilla strips, avocado and lime.
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can black beans, rinsed and drained
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
2 limes, 1 juiced and 1 cut into wedges
instructions: Put the chicken, onion, garlic, jalapeno, black beans, tomatoes with their juices, corn, broth, cumin, chili powder, paprika, oregano and salt in the slow cooker and stir.
Cover and cook on low for 6 hours, or on high for 3 hours, until the chicken shreds easily.
Near the end, preheat the oven to 400°F. Toss the tortilla strips with the oil and a pinch of salt on a baking sheet and bake for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring once, until crisp and golden.
Lift the chicken out, shred it with two forks and return it to the pot. Stir in the lime juice and most of the cilantro, then taste for salt.
Ladle into bowls and top with the tortilla strips, avocado, sour cream, the rest of the cilantro and a lime wedge.
notes: Thighs stay juicy through the long cook. Breasts work too, but cook them on low for only 4 hours. Keep the tortilla strips separate so they stay crisp. The soup keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes well without the toppings.

name: Slow Cooker Pulled Pork with Slaw
description: Spice-rubbed pork shoulder cooked until it falls apart, tossed with barbecue sauce and piled onto buns under a tangy, crunchy slaw.
ingredients: 4 lb boneless pork shoulder, trimmed of excess fat
2 tbsp apple cider vinegar, for the slaw
instructions: Mix the brown sugar, paprika, salt, cumin, garlic powder and pepper, and rub it all over the pork.
Scatter the onion in the slow cooker, set the pork on top and pour the broth and 1/4 cup vinegar around it.
Cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours, until the pork pulls apart easily with a fork.
Lift out the pork and shred it with two forks, throwing away any large pieces of fat. Skim the fat from the cooking liquid.
Return the pork to the slow cooker with the barbecue sauce and about 1 cup of the cooking liquid, toss well and keep warm.
For the slaw, whisk the mayonnaise, 2 tbsp vinegar, honey and a pinch of salt, then toss with the cabbage and carrots. Let it sit for at least 15 minutes to soften slightly.
Pile the pork onto the toasted buns and top with slaw.
notes: Use pork shoulder (sometimes sold as Boston butt); leaner loin dries out. The pork releases plenty of liquid, so don't add more. Shredded pork freezes well in its juices for up to 3 months. Dress the slaw no more than a few hours ahead.

name: Slow Cooker Sweet Potato Black Bean Chili
description: A hearty, smoky vegetarian chili where soft sweet potato balances the heat of chipotle and chili powder.
ingredients: 2 sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into 3/4-inch cubes
2 (15 oz) cans black beans, rinsed and drained
1 chipotle chile in adobo sauce, minced (optional)
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Put the sweet potatoes, onion, bell pepper, garlic, beans, tomatoes, broth, chipotle, chili powder, cumin, paprika, oregano and salt in the slow cooker and stir well.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours, or on high for 4 hours, until the sweet potatoes are tender.
Mash some of the sweet potato and beans against the side of the pot to thicken the chili. If it's still thin, cook uncovered on high for 20 minutes.
Stir in the lime juice, taste and adjust the salt, and serve topped with cilantro, cheddar and sour cream.
notes: Leave out the cheese and sour cream, or use plant-based ones, to make it vegan. The chipotle adds smoky heat; leave it out for a milder chili. Keeps 5 days in the fridge and freezes well.

name: Fish Tacos with Cabbage Slaw
description: Spiced, pan-seared cod in charred corn tortillas with a bright lime slaw and a cool lime crema.
ingredients: 3 limes, 2 juiced and 1 cut into wedges
instructions: Stir the sour cream with 1 tbsp of the lime juice and a pinch of salt to make the crema. Toss the cabbage and cilantro with the rest of the lime juice and 1/2 tsp salt, and set both aside.
Pat the cod dry and season both sides with the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and the remaining 1 tsp salt.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the cod for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until it is opaque and flakes easily (145°F). Break it into large flakes.
Meanwhile, warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or over a gas flame for about 30 seconds per side, until lightly charred, and wrap them in a towel.
Fill the tortillas with the fish and slaw, drizzle with the crema, and serve with lime wedges and jalapeno.
notes: Any firm white fish works, such as halibut, haddock or tilapia (tilapia needs only 2 to 3 minutes per side). Stack two tortillas per taco if yours tear easily.

name: Chicken Cabbage Rice Bowls
description: Ginger-garlic glazed chicken thighs over brown rice with a quick, tangy cabbage and carrot slaw.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
instructions: Bring the rice, water and a pinch of salt to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 40 to 45 minutes, until tender. Let it stand off the heat, covered, for 10 minutes.
While the rice cooks, toss the cabbage and carrots with 2 tbsp of the vinegar, 1 tsp of the sesame oil and the salt, and set aside to lightly pickle.
Whisk the soy sauce, honey, the remaining 1 tbsp vinegar, garlic, ginger, cornstarch and red pepper flakes in a small bowl.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken in one layer and cook without stirring for 3 minutes, then stir and cook for 3 to 4 minutes more, until browned and cooked through (165°F).
Pour in the sauce and cook, stirring, for 1 to 2 minutes, until it thickens and glazes the chicken. Stir in the remaining 1 tsp sesame oil.
Divide the rice among bowls and top with the chicken, slaw, green onions and sesame seeds.
notes: Cook the rice a day ahead and this is a 20-minute dinner. The slaw keeps 3 days and gets better as it sits. Cubed firm tofu works in place of the chicken; brown it well before adding the sauce.

name: Kale, Sausage and White Bean Soup
description: A brothy Tuscan-style soup with browned Italian sausage, creamy white beans and tender kale, brightened with lemon and parmesan.
ingredients: 2 (15 oz) cans cannellini beans, rinsed and drained
1 bunch lacinato kale, stems removed and leaves chopped
1/2 cup grated parmesan, plus more for serving
1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the sausage and cook, breaking it up, until browned, about 6 minutes.
Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook until softened, about 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic and red pepper flakes for 1 minute.
Add the broth and beans and scrape up the browned bits. Mash about a cup of the beans against the side of the pot to give the soup body. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the kale and simmer for 5 to 7 minutes, until tender.
Off the heat, stir in the parmesan and lemon juice. Season with the salt and pepper and serve with more parmesan.
notes: Drop a parmesan rind in with the broth for extra savoury depth, and fish it out before serving. Use hot Italian sausage and skip the pepper flakes if you like heat. Keeps 4 days in the fridge; the kale softens more as it reheats.

name: Sheet-Pan Salmon with Broccoli
description: Garlic and lemon salmon roasted on one pan with crisp-edged broccoli, served over fluffy quinoa.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb salmon fillet, cut into 4 pieces
1 lemon, zested and cut into wedges
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Bring the quinoa, water and a pinch of salt to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes. Let it stand, covered, for 5 minutes and fluff with a fork.
Meanwhile, toss the broccoli on a large rimmed baking sheet with 2 tbsp of the oil, 1/2 tsp salt and the red pepper flakes. Roast for 10 minutes.
Mix the remaining 1 tbsp oil with the garlic and lemon zest. Pat the salmon dry and season it with the remaining 3/4 tsp salt and the pepper.

Push the broccoli to the edges of the pan, lay the salmon skin side down in the middle and spoon the garlic oil over it. Roast for 10 to 12 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily and reads 125 to 130°F in the thickest part.
Squeeze lemon wedges over everything, scatter with dill and serve with the quinoa.
notes: Thin fillets cook faster, so check them at 8 minutes. Salmon keeps cooking off the heat, so take it out while the centre is still slightly translucent. Leftovers are good cold over the quinoa with a squeeze of lemon.

name: Summer Tomato Basil Pasta
description: Whole wheat spaghetti tossed with cherry tomatoes blistered until saucy, zucchini, garlic, torn basil and parmesan.
ingredients: 1 1/4 tsp kosher salt, plus more for the pasta water
1/2 cup grated parmesan, plus more for serving
instructions: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Cook the pasta until 1 minute short of the package time, then scoop out 1 cup of the cooking water before draining.
While the pasta cooks, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the garlic and red pepper flakes for 1 to 2 minutes, until the garlic is pale golden.

Raise the heat to medium-high, add the zucchini and cook for 3 minutes. Add the tomatoes and salt and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the tomatoes burst and turn saucy. Press a few with your spoon to help them along.
Add the drained pasta and 1/2 cup of the pasta water and toss over the heat for 1 to 2 minutes, adding more water as needed, until the sauce is glossy and clings to the pasta.
Off the heat, toss in the parmesan, most of the basil and the pepper. Serve with the remaining basil and more parmesan.
notes: Best in late summer, when tomatoes are at their sweetest. The starchy pasta water is what turns the tomatoes into a sauce, so don't skip it. Traditional parmesan is made with animal rennet; use a vegetarian hard cheese if that matters to you.

name: Mushroom Barley Skillet
description: Creamy, risotto-style pearl barley with deeply browned mushrooms, thyme, wilted spinach and parmesan.
instructions: Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat. Spread the mushrooms in an even layer and cook without stirring for 4 minutes, then stir and cook for 4 minutes more, until well browned. Season with 1/2 tsp salt and move them to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium, add the onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, thyme and barley and toast for 2 minutes.

Pour in the wine, if using, and let it bubble away. Add 4 cups of the broth and the remaining salt, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 35 to 40 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the barley is tender but still chewy. Add the rest of the broth if it looks dry.
Stir in the mushrooms and spinach and cook for 2 minutes, until the spinach wilts.
Off the heat, stir in the butter, parmesan, lemon juice and pepper. It should be creamy and loose; add a splash of broth or water if it's stiff.
notes: Don't crowd or stir the mushrooms early: leaving them alone is what browns them. Quick-cooking barley cuts the simmer to about 12 minutes. Use a rennet-free hard cheese for a strictly vegetarian dish. Leftovers thicken in the fridge, so loosen them with broth when reheating.

name: Butternut Squash Lentil Curry
description: A warming coconut curry of red lentils and sweet butternut squash with ginger, garlic and spinach, finished with lime.
ingredients: 1 butternut squash (about 2 lb), peeled and cut into 3/4-inch cubes
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion with 1/2 tsp of the salt until soft and golden, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, curry powder and cumin and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.

Add the squash, lentils, coconut milk, tomatoes, broth and the remaining salt. Bring to a boil, then partly cover and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils have broken down and the squash is tender.
Meanwhile, cook the rice according to the package directions.
Stir the spinach into the curry until it wilts, about 2 minutes, then add the lime juice. Taste for salt. The curry should be thick; add a splash of water if it's stiff.
Serve over the rice, topped with cilantro.
notes: Use red lentils: they melt into the sauce, while green or brown ones stay whole and take longer. Curry powders vary in heat, so add a pinch of cayenne or a sliced green chili if yours is mild. Freezes well for up to 3 months.

name: Turkey Zucchini Skillet
description: Taco-spiced ground turkey with zucchini, peppers and black beans, melted together with cheddar and served in warm tortillas.
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can black beans, rinsed and drained
instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the turkey and cook, breaking it up, until browned with no pink left, about 6 minutes.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook for 4 minutes. Add the zucchini, garlic, chili powder, cumin, paprika and salt and cook for 3 to 4 minutes more, until the zucchini is just tender.
Stir in the beans and tomatoes and simmer for 3 minutes, until most of the liquid has cooked off.
Scatter the cheddar over the top, cover and turn off the heat. Let it stand for 2 minutes to melt.
Spoon into the warm tortillas and finish with green onions and a squeeze of lime.
notes: Ground turkey that is 93% lean or less stays moister than extra-lean. Skip the tortillas and serve it over rice or greens if you prefer. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

name: Chickpea Shakshuka
description: Eggs gently poached in a cumin-spiced tomato sauce with chickpeas and spinach, topped with feta and served with toast for dipping.
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can chickpeas, rinsed and drained
4 slices crusty bread, toasted, for serving
instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper until soft, about 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika and red pepper flakes for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, chickpeas and salt and simmer for 8 minutes, until slightly thickened. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Make 6 wells in the sauce with a spoon and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook on medium-low for 5 to 7 minutes, until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny.
Scatter with the feta and parsley and serve straight from the pan with the toast.
notes: Take the pan off the heat as soon as the whites are set, because the yolks keep cooking. The sauce can be made up to 3 days ahead; reheat it until bubbling before adding the eggs.

name: Sheet-Pan Lemon Herb Chicken with Potatoes and Green Beans
description: Crisp-skinned chicken thighs roasted with lemon, garlic and herbs over golden potatoes, with green beans added for the last stretch.
ingredients: 2 lemons, 1 zested and juiced and 1 thinly sliced
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Mix 2 tbsp of the oil with the garlic, lemon zest and juice, oregano, thyme, 1 1/2 tsp of the salt and the pepper.
Toss the potatoes with half the herb mixture on a large rimmed baking sheet. Pat the chicken dry, rub it with the rest, and nestle it skin side up among the potatoes with the lemon slices.
Roast for 25 minutes.

Toss the green beans with the remaining 1 tbsp oil and 1/2 tsp salt and scatter them around the chicken. Roast for 15 to 20 minutes more, until the skin is crisp, the chicken reads 175°F and the potatoes are golden.
Rest for 5 minutes, then spoon the pan juices over everything and sprinkle with parsley.
notes: Bone-in thighs are very forgiving and hard to overcook. With boneless thighs, roast everything together for about 25 minutes in all. If the pan is crowded, use two, or the potatoes will steam instead of browning.

name: Apple Cinnamon Oatmeal
description: Creamy stovetop oats cooked in milk, topped with buttery cinnamon apples, maple syrup and toasted walnuts.
instructions: Melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Cook the apple with half the cinnamon for 3 to 4 minutes, until just soft, then spoon half of it out for the topping.
Add the oats, milk, water, salt and the remaining cinnamon to the pan. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Stir in the maple syrup and let it stand off the heat for 1 minute. Serve topped with the reserved apple and the walnuts.
notes: Use all milk for richer oatmeal, or all water for a lighter bowl. The salt matters: without it oatmeal tastes flat. Steel-cut oats need 3 cups of liquid and about 25 minutes.

name: Kale and Egg Scramble
description: Soft, creamy scrambled eggs folded with garlicky wilted kale and salty feta, with toast on the side.
ingredients: 1/4 bunch kale, stems removed and leaves chopped
instructions: Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add the kale and garlic with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring, for 3 minutes, until wilted and bright green. Move it to a plate.
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper until no streaks remain.
Melt the butter in the same pan over medium-low heat. Add the eggs and stir slowly with a spatula for 2 to 3 minutes, pulling them into soft curds.
When the eggs are almost set but still glossy, fold in the kale and feta. Serve right away with the toast.
notes: Low heat and steady stirring give soft, creamy eggs; take them off while they still look slightly wet. Spinach or chard work in place of the kale (spinach needs only 1 minute).

name: Yogurt Berry Parfait
description: Layers of thick Greek yogurt, fresh blueberries and crunchy honey-cinnamon toasted oats.
ingredients: 1 tbsp honey, plus more for serving
instructions: Melt the butter in a small skillet over medium heat. Add the oats, cinnamon and salt and toast, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes, until golden and nutty.
Drizzle in the honey and stir for 1 minute, until the oats clump, then spread them on a plate to cool and crisp, about 5 minutes.
Layer the yogurt, blueberries and toasted oats in two glasses, finishing with oats and a little extra honey.
notes: Toast a big batch of oats and keep them in a jar for up to 2 weeks. Add the oats just before eating so they stay crunchy. Any berries, or diced peaches, work in place of blueberries.

name: Make-Ahead Veggie Egg Muffins
description: Fluffy baked egg cups packed with spinach, red pepper, green onion and cheddar, made once for a week of grab-and-go breakfasts.
ingredients: 1 tbsp olive oil, plus more for the pan
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F and oil a 12-cup muffin tin well.

Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the bell pepper for 4 minutes, until soft. Add the spinach and cook for 1 minute, until wilted, then let it cool slightly. Cooking the vegetables first keeps the muffins from turning watery.
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt, pepper and garlic powder until smooth.
Divide the vegetables, green onions and cheddar among the cups, then pour in the egg mixture until each is about three-quarters full.
Bake for 20 to 22 minutes, until puffed and set in the centre. Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then run a knife around each one to release it.
notes: Keep in the fridge for up to 4 days or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat in the microwave for 30 to 45 seconds. Silicone or parchment liners make them easiest to release.

name: Apple Slices with Nut Butter
description: Crisp apple slices with creamy peanut butter for dipping, dusted with cinnamon and a pinch of flaky salt.
instructions: Toss the apple slices with the lemon juice and a splash of water so they don't brown.
Stir the peanut butter until smooth. If it's stiff, warm it in the microwave for 10 seconds so it's easy to dip.
Arrange the slices on a plate, sprinkle with the cinnamon, and serve with the peanut butter topped with a pinch of flaky salt.
notes: Crisp, sweet-tart apples such as Honeycrisp or Pink Lady are best. Any nut or seed butter works; sunflower seed butter keeps it nut-free. The lemon-tossed slices keep 1 day in the fridge.

name: Hummus and Veggie Plate
description: Silky homemade hummus whipped with tahini, lemon and garlic, served with crunchy carrots, cucumber and red pepper.
ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil, plus more for serving
1 (15 oz) can chickpeas, rinsed and drained
1 red bell pepper, cut into strips
instructions: Blend the tahini and lemon juice in a food processor for 1 minute, until thick and pale.
Add the garlic, olive oil, cumin and salt and blend for 30 seconds, scraping down the sides.
Add the chickpeas and blend for 2 minutes, drizzling in the ice water, until very smooth and fluffy. Taste and add more salt or lemon if needed.
Spread the hummus in a shallow bowl, swirl with olive oil and dust with paprika. Serve with the carrots, cucumber and pepper.
notes: Whipping the tahini and lemon first and adding ice water make the hummus light and creamy. For extra-smooth hummus, simmer the chickpeas in water with 1/2 tsp baking soda for 15 minutes and rinse them before blending. Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

name: Roasted Chickpeas
description: Crunchy oven-roasted chickpeas tossed with smoked paprika, garlic and cumin while still hot.
ingredients: 2 (15 oz) cans chickpeas, rinsed and drained
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle.
Dry the chickpeas very well with a clean towel, rubbing off any loose skins. The drier they are, the crunchier they get.
Toss them with the oil and salt, spread them in one layer on a rimmed baking sheet, and roast for 25 to 30 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until deep golden and crunchy.
Mix the paprika, garlic powder and cumin and toss with the hot chickpeas. Let them cool on the pan for 10 minutes; they crisp more as they cool.
notes: The spices go on after roasting so they don't burn. Keep them loosely covered at room temperature and eat within 2 days; the fridge makes them soft. Re-crisp at 350°F for 5 minutes.

name: Cheddar and Pear Plate
description: Sharp cheddar and juicy pear with honey-drizzled toasted walnuts and whole grain crackers.
instructions: Take the cheddar out of the fridge 20 minutes before serving so its flavour comes through.
Toast the walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, shaking the pan, until fragrant. Let them cool.
Arrange the cheddar, pears, walnuts and crackers on a board and drizzle the honey over the walnuts and cheese.
notes: Slice the pears just before serving, or toss them with a little lemon juice to keep them pale. Crisp apples or grapes work in place of the pears.

name: Baked Cinnamon Apples
description: Whole apples stuffed with a buttery oat, brown sugar and walnut crumble and baked until tender in their own cinnamon syrup.
ingredients: 4 firm apples, such as Honeycrisp or Braeburn
1 cup plain Greek yogurt, for serving
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Core the apples from the top with a melon baller or small spoon, leaving the bottoms intact so the filling stays in. Peel a thin strip of skin around the top of each so they don't split.
Rub the oats, brown sugar, walnuts, cinnamon, salt and butter together with your fingers until crumbly, and pack the mixture into the apples, mounding it on top.
Stand the apples in a baking dish just big enough to hold them and pour the hot water around them.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes, basting with the pan juices once or twice, until a knife slides easily into the apples. Cover loosely with foil if the tops brown too fast.
Cool for 10 minutes and serve with the yogurt and a spoonful of the pan syrup.
notes: Use apples that hold their shape, such as Honeycrisp, Braeburn or Pink Lady; soft ones like McIntosh collapse. Leftovers reheat well and make a good breakfast.

name: Banana Oat Cookies
description: Soft, chewy cookies sweetened with ripe banana, with peanut butter, cinnamon and dark chocolate chips. No flour or added sugar in the dough.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Mash the bananas well in a bowl, then stir in the peanut butter, vanilla, cinnamon and salt until smooth.
Stir in the oats and chocolate chips and let the dough rest for 10 minutes so the oats soften and soak up the banana.
Scoop heaping tablespoons onto the baking sheet 1 inch apart and flatten each to about 1/2 inch thick, because they won't spread.
Bake for 14 to 16 minutes, until golden underneath and set on top. Cool on the pan for 10 minutes; they firm up as they cool.
notes: The riper the bananas, the sweeter the cookies: ones covered in brown spots are best. They're soft and cakey rather than crisp. Keep them in the fridge for up to 5 days, or freeze for 2 months.

name: Frozen Yogurt Berry Bark
description: Honey-sweetened Greek yogurt spread thin, studded with strawberries, blueberries and dark chocolate, then frozen and broken into shards.
ingredients: 1 cup strawberries, hulled, diced and patted dry
instructions: Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment.
Stir the yogurt, honey, vanilla and salt until smooth. Taste it: it should be a little sweeter than you'd like, because freezing dulls sweetness.
Spread the yogurt about 1/4 inch thick on the parchment, in a rectangle roughly 9 by 13 inches.
Scatter the strawberries, blueberries and chocolate chips over the top and press them in lightly.
Freeze for at least 3 hours, until firm, then break into pieces.
notes: Whole-milk Greek yogurt freezes creamier and less icy than low-fat. Drying the berries well stops ice crystals forming around them. Keep the pieces in a freezer bag for up to 1 month and serve them straight from the freezer, as they soften within 5 minutes.

name: Mint Lemonade
description: Fresh-squeezed lemonade sweetened with a mint-infused honey syrup: tart, cooling and not too sweet.
ingredients: 6 lemons, juiced (about 1 cup), plus slices for serving
1 bunch mint, plus sprigs for serving
instructions: Stir the honey into the hot water until it dissolves. Bruise a big handful of mint leaves in your hands, add them to the syrup and steep for 10 minutes.
Strain the mint syrup into a pitcher, pressing on the leaves, and stir in the lemon juice and cold water.
Taste and balance it with a little more water or honey. Chill until cold, or serve right away over plenty of ice.
Garnish each glass with a mint sprig and a lemon slice.
notes: Roll the lemons firmly on the counter before cutting to get more juice. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; add fresh mint sprigs just before serving so they stay bright. Top each glass with club soda for a sparkling version.

name: Strawberry Banana Smoothie
description: A thick, creamy smoothie of strawberries, frozen banana and Greek yogurt.
instructions: Pour the milk into the blender first, then add the yogurt, strawberries, frozen banana, honey and ice.
Blend on high for 45 to 60 seconds, until completely smooth. Add a splash more milk if it's too thick to pour.
Taste, add a little more honey if the berries were tart, and serve right away.
notes: Freeze ripe banana slices on a tray, then keep them in a bag: frozen banana makes the smoothie thick and cold without watering it down. Liquid first helps the blender start smoothly. Swap in any berries.

name: Cucumber Ginger Cooler
description: A crisp, sparkling cooler of fresh cucumber juice with ginger, lime, mint and a touch of honey.
ingredients: 1/4 bunch mint, plus sprigs for serving
instructions: Blend the cucumber, ginger, lime juice, honey, mint leaves and cold water for about 1 minute, until completely smooth.
Strain through a fine sieve into a pitcher, pressing on the pulp. You should have about 1 1/2 cups of juice.
Chill until ready to serve, for up to 1 day.
Fill four glasses with ice, pour in the cucumber juice and top each with club soda. Stir gently and garnish with a mint sprig.
notes: Add the club soda at the last moment so it stays fizzy. Use more or less ginger to taste; the flavour gets stronger as the juice sits.
